questions.q: What will a judge do when he reaches a judgement in a dispute between two men in court?
questions.a: He will declare the righteous as innocent and declare the wicked as guilty.

questions.q: Why will a judge limit the number of blows a man will receive?
questions.a: The judge will order the number of blows to not exceed 40 blows so the man will not be humiliated.

questions.q: What safeguard did Yahweh institute so that the name of a man would not disappear from Israel?
questions.a: If a man dies without having a son, his brother must take the dead man’s widow as his wife so that the firstborn she bears will carry on the name of that man’s dead brother.

questions.q: What punishment did Yahweh allow if the man’s brother did not wish to take his brother’s wife?
questions.a: The brother’s wife will take off his sandal in the presence of the elders, spit in his face, and tell him that this is what is done when a man refuses to preserve his brother’s family line.

questions.q: What would cause a wife to have one of her hands cut off?
questions.a: If two men were fighting and the wife of one of the men grabs the private part of the other man in an attempt to rescue her husband, then her hand must be cut off.

questions.q: What kind of dishonest act is disgusting to Yahweh?
questions.a: It is disgusting to Yahweh when a man has a large and a small weight to measure rather than a correct weight.

questions.q: Why must the people of Israel wipe out the memory of Amalek?
questions.a: Amalek did not honor God when Amalek met Israel on the road and attacked those who were faint and weary at the rear as they came out of Egypt.

commentary.text: The ox that treadeth the corn.

Verses 1–3 Every punishment should be with solemnity, that those who see it may be filled with dread, and be warned not to offend in like manner. And though the criminals must be shamed as well as put to pain, for their warning and disgrace, yet care should be taken that they do not appear totally vile. Happy those who are chastened of the Lord to humble them, that they should not be condemned with the world to destruction.

This is a charge to husbandmen. It teaches us to make much of the animals that serve us. But we must learn, not only to be just, but kind to all who are employed for the good of our better part, our souls, 1Co 9:9.
The custom here regulated seems to have been in the Jewish law in order to keep inheritances distinct; now it is unlawful.

Dishonest gain always brings a curse on men's property, families, and souls. Happy those who judge themselves, repent of and forsake their sins, and put away evil things, that they may not be condemned of the Lord.

Let every persecutor and injurer of God's people take warning from the case of the Amalekites. The longer it is before judgement comes, the more dreadful will it be at last. Amalek may remind us of the foes of our souls. May we be enabled to slay all our lusts, all the corruptions both within and without, all the powers of darkness and of the world, which oppose our way to the blessed Saviour.
